messages:
alex: Heads-up: restore jobs alerting with KMS DecryptFailure for a few snapshots in prod-us-west-2. Quick grep shows those objects have no SSE metadata.
rachel: How many objects and which tenants?
alex: 9 objects across tenants t-7 and t-9, all uploaded in the last 6h.
diego: Any code changes related to presigns or the uploader?
alex: Yes 3h ago we rolled a change simplifying presign conditions to try to fix a multipart abort bug. Looks like the final multipart-complete presign no longer forces SSE headers.
infra: deploy-bot: presign-service v1.6.0 deployed to prod-us-west-2 at 1777769000.
kms-bot: Incident filed: ENCOPS-2026-312. Initial severity: medium. Suggested mitigations: block presign, run detection, plan rewrap.
rachel: Immediate steps: 1) disable presign issuance for multipart finalizations, 2) add bucket policy to deny PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption on /snapshots/*, 3) run detection over last 12h.
diego: For rewraps we need to ensure Encrypt is called with the same encryption context that was used originally. Check CloudTrail for Encrypt events to capture context values.
alex: Good point. Our encrypt pipeline stores encryption context in snapshot metadata but the object metadata was missing SSE so restore path bails before using context. Rewrap job must set SSE-KMS and encryption-context accordingly.
rachel: RBAC question: who gets kms:Encrypt for the rewrap job? We should avoid granting broad permissions. Use ephemeral grants scoped to the specific CMKs and with TTL.
diego: Agreed. infra can spin an ephemeral grant automation. We also need to ensure the grant principal matches the uploader role ARN used by the rewrap process.
infra: I can automate grant creation. Will require a short maintenance window to run rewraps.
kms-bot: Recommended: use aws kms create-grant with operations: Encrypt,Decrypt,RetireGrant, and set GranteePrincipal to the rewrap principal. Limit TTL via scheduled revoke.
alex: Audit / compliance: export list of affected objects, upload events, presign issuer and agent instance IDs. Compliance will want CloudTrail and S3 metadata snapshots.
rachel: Post-mortem items: - Re-introduce unit tests for presign generator that assert SSE conditions for both single-part and multipart flows. - Add CI lint gate to detect removal of presign header checks. - Add SIEM rule to alert on object creations under /snapshots/ where SSE metadata is missing.
diego: Defensive fix: patch presign generator to always include condition: "x-amz-server-side-encryption":"aws:kms" and require the key-id/encryption-context when applicable. Also add a runtime check at upload-proxy to reject uploads that don't match the presign conditions.
infra: Temporary mitigation: apply S3 bucket policy to deny non-SSE puts for snapshot prefix. Example deny condition posted in ticket.
kms-bot: Note: do NOT edit customer CMKs' key policies without explicit approval. Use grants for remediation wherever possible.
alex: For small object counts we will copy-object -> put-object with SSE-KMS under rewrap principal after ephemeral grant. For larger counts we'll coordinate with tenant owners for throttled rewrap or snapshot roll-forward decisions.
rachel: Who owns the rewrap run? alex volunteers for detection and small rewraps; infra to provide grant automation; diego to review encryption-context handling.
infra: I'll schedule a 2hr window tonight to run the small rewrap queue and post grant IDs in the incident ticket.
kms-bot: Update: presign issuance disabled, bucket policy applied, detection scan scheduled. Monitoring enabled.
alex: I'll attach the detection results and a short runbook after rewrap completes. Keep compliance looped in if any regulated tenant is affected.
rachel: Thanks team. Keep notes concise in the incident ticket.
diego: :thumbsup:
